titulo_es: Rico y feliz: alimentación y emociones
estandares: Hablo de alimentación y bienestar comparando opciones y expresando preferencias. Describo emociones y estados de ánimo con vocabulario preciso.
competencias: Distinguir sustantivos contables e incontables; preguntar por cantidades; comparar y establecer superlativos con adjetivos regulares e irregulares; expresar gustos, emociones y hábitos saludables.
componentes: Pensamiento crítico, comunicación, colaboración y creatividad.

proyecto.descripcion_es: En grupos, los estudiantes diseñan el menú de una semana y lo presentan comparando platos (healthier, the most nutritious) y explicando cómo se sienten con cada tipo de comida.
proyecto.descripcion_en: In groups, students design a one-week menu and present it comparing dishes (healthier, the most nutritious) and explaining how each type of food makes them feel.

lecciones.content_es:
La diferencia

  • Contables: se pueden contar y tienen plural. an apple, two apples
  • Incontables: no se cuentan en unidades y no tienen plural. rice, water, milk, bread, sugar, money, information, advice

Cómo medir los incontables

Con recipientes o porciones: a glass of water, a piece of bread, a cup of coffee, a bottle of milk, a kilo of rice, a slice of cheese.

Concordancia

Los incontables llevan verbo en singular: The news is good. · The information is useful.

Trampa

Algunas palabras que en español son contables, en inglés no lo son: advice, furniture, homework, bread, money.
lecciones.content_en:
The difference

  • Countable: they can be counted and have a plural. an apple, two apples
  • Uncountable: they are not counted in units and have no plural. rice, water, milk, bread, sugar, money, information, advice

How to measure uncountables

With containers or portions: a glass of water, a piece of bread, a cup of coffee, a bottle of milk, a kilo of rice, a slice of cheese.

Agreement

Uncountables take a singular verb: The news is good. · The information is useful.

Trap

Some words that are countable in Spanish are not in English: advice, furniture, homework, bread, money.

lecciones.t: How much / How many y cuantificadores en preguntas
lecciones.t_en: How much / How many and quantifiers in questions
lecciones.content_es:
La pregunta correcta

  • How many + contable plural: How many eggs do we need?
  • How much + incontable: How much milk is there?

Respuestas típicas

A lot. / Not much. / Only a few. / None. / Two kilos.

Cuantificadores en preguntas y negaciones

  • any: Do we have any sugar? · There isn't any juice.
  • enough: Is there enough rice for everyone?
  • too much / too many (demasiado): You eat too much sugar. / Too many cookies.

Ojo

How much también sirve para preguntar precios: How much is it?
lecciones.content_en:
The right question

  • How many + plural countable: How many eggs do we need?
  • How much + uncountable: How much milk is there?

Typical answers

A lot. / Not much. / Only a few. / None. / Two kilos.

Quantifiers in questions and negatives

  • any: Do we have any sugar? · There isn't any juice.
  • enough: Is there enough rice for everyone?
  • too much / too many: You eat too much sugar. / Too many cookies.

Careful

How much is also used to ask prices: How much is it?

lecciones.content_es:
Comparar dos cosas

Estructura: adjetivo comparativo + than. Apples are healthier than chips.

Cómo se forman

  • Adjetivos cortos (1 sílaba) → -er: tall → taller, cheap → cheaper
  • Termina en -e → solo -r: large → larger
  • Consonante + y → -ier: happy → happier, healthy → healthier
  • Consonante-vocal-consonante corta → se dobla: big → bigger, hot → hotter
  • Adjetivos largos (2+ sílabas) → more + adjetivo: more expensive, more interesting

Otras comparaciones

  • Igualdad: as … as — She is as tall as her brother.
  • Desigualdad: not as … as — Soda isn't as healthy as water.
lecciones.content_en:
Comparing two things

Structure: comparative adjective + than. Apples are healthier than chips.

How they are formed

  • Short adjectives (1 syllable) → -er: tall → taller, cheap → cheaper
  • Ending in -e → just -r: large → larger
  • Consonant + y → -ier: happy → happier, healthy → healthier
  • Short consonant-vowel-consonant → double it: big → bigger, hot → hotter
  • Long adjectives (2+ syllables) → more + adjective: more expensive, more interesting

Other comparisons

  • Equality: as … as — She is as tall as her brother.
  • Inequality: not as … as — Soda isn't as healthy as water.

lecciones.content_es:
El máximo del grupo

Estructura: the + superlativo. This is the best restaurant in town.

Cómo se forman

  • Cortos → the -est: tall → the tallest, big → the biggest
  • Consonante + y → the -iest: happy → the happiest
  • Largos → the most + adjetivo: the most delicious

El artículo the es obligatorio

Siempre se dice the tallest, no tallest solo.

Complementos frecuentes

in + lugar: the biggest city in Colombia.
of + grupo: the youngest of my cousins.
Con presente perfecto: the best movie I have ever seen.
lecciones.content_en:
The top of the group

Structure: the + superlative. This is the best restaurant in town.

How they are formed

  • Short → the -est: tall → the tallest, big → the biggest
  • Consonant + y → the -iest: happy → the happiest
  • Long → the most + adjective: the most delicious

The article the is compulsory

We always say the tallest, never just tallest.

Frequent complements

in + place: the biggest city in Colombia.
of + group: the youngest of my cousins.
With the present perfect: the best movie I have ever seen.

lecciones.content_es:
Los que no siguen la regla

  • good → better → the best
  • bad → worse → the worst
  • far → farther / further → the farthest / the furthest
  • little → less → the least
  • much / many → more → the most

Errores comunes

No existe gooder, more better ni baddest. Se dice better than y the worst.

En contexto

Vegetables are better for you than fried food.
That was the worst day of my life.
I eat less sugar now.
lecciones.content_en:
The ones that break the rule

  • good → better → the best
  • bad → worse → the worst
  • far → farther / further → the farthest / the furthest
  • little → less → the least
  • much / many → more → the most

Common mistakes

There is no gooder, more better or baddest. We say better than and the worst.

In context

Vegetables are better for you than fried food.
That was the worst day of my life.
I eat less sugar now.

lecciones.t: El alfabeto y el deletreo aplicado
lecciones.t_en: The alphabet and spelling in practice
lecciones.content_es:
Deletrear en situaciones reales

Se usa para dar tu nombre, un correo o un ingrediente que el otro no conoce.

  • My name is Yeimi. Y-E-I-M-I.
  • My email is ana punto lopez arroba mail punto com → ana dot lopez at mail dot com.

Símbolos

@ = at · . = dot · _ = underscore · - = hyphen o dash · / = slash.

Palabras difíciles de comida

vegetable, restaurant, chocolate, sandwich, receipt, biscuit — todas tienen letras que no se pronuncian.

Frases: Could you spell that, please? · How do you spell it? · It's spelled with a double L.
lecciones.content_en:
Spelling in real situations

You use it to give your name, an email address or an ingredient the other person does not know.

  • My name is Yeimi. Y-E-I-M-I.
  • My email is ana dot lopez at mail dot com.

Symbols

@ = at · . = dot · _ = underscore · - = hyphen or dash · / = slash.

Tricky food words

vegetable, restaurant, chocolate, sandwich, receipt, biscuit — they all have silent letters.

Phrases: Could you spell that, please? · How do you spell it? · It's spelled with a double L.

lecciones.content_es:
Grupos de alimentos

fruits: apple, banana, orange, grapes, pineapple, watermelon.
vegetables: carrot, tomato, onion, lettuce, potato, spinach.
proteins: chicken, beef, pork, fish, eggs, beans, lentils.
dairy: milk, cheese, yogurt, butter.
grains: rice, pasta, bread, cereal, corn.

Formas de preparar

fried (frito), boiled (hervido), baked (al horno), grilled (a la parrilla), raw (crudo), roasted (asado).

Sabores

sweet, salty, sour (ácido), bitter (amargo), spicy (picante), tasty / delicious.

Alimentación saludable

A balanced diet includes fruits, vegetables and proteins. You should avoid fried food and sugary drinks.

lecciones.content_es:
Emociones básicas

happy, sad, angry, scared, surprised, tired, excited (emocionado), nervous, bored (aburrido), worried (preocupado), proud (orgulloso), relaxed, confused, disappointed (decepcionado).

-ed vs -ing

El adjetivo en -ed describe cómo te sientes; el que termina en -ing describe la causa:

  • I am bored. (yo me aburro) vs. The class is boring. (la clase aburre)
  • I'm interested in music vs. Music is interesting

Expresar cómo te sientes

How do you feel? — I feel great. / I'm a bit nervous. / I'm really excited about the trip.
lecciones.content_en:
Basic emotions

happy, sad, angry, scared, surprised, tired, excited, nervous, bored, worried, proud, relaxed, confused, disappointed.

-ed vs -ing

The -ed adjective describes how you feel; the -ing one describes the cause:

  • I am bored. vs. The class is boring.
  • I'm interested in music vs. Music is interesting

Expressing how you feel

How do you feel? — I feel great. / I'm a bit nervous. / I'm really excited about the trip.

repaso.resumen_es:
Lo esencial del periodo

El periodo combina cantidad y comparación. Primero decides si el sustantivo es contable o incontable; eso determina el cuantificador y la pregunta (how many / how much). Después comparas con -er / more … than y marcas el máximo con the -est / the most.

Puntos gramaticales

  • Incontables: sin plural, verbo en singular, se miden con a piece of, a glass of.
  • Comparativo: adjetivo corto + -er + than; adjetivo largo con more.
  • Superlativo: siempre con the.
  • Irregulares: good-better-the best, bad-worse-the worst, little-less-the least.

Vocabulario

Deletreo y símbolos (@ at, . dot, _ underscore), grupos de alimentos, formas de preparación, sabores y emociones con -ed / -ing.
repaso.resumen_en:
The core of the term

The term combines quantity and comparison. First you decide whether the noun is countable or uncountable; that determines the quantifier and the question (how many / how much). Then you compare with -er / more … than and mark the top with the -est / the most.

Grammar points

  • Uncountables: no plural, singular verb, measured with a piece of, a glass of.
  • Comparative: short adjective + -er + than; long adjective with more.
  • Superlative: always with the.
  • Irregulars: good-better-the best, bad-worse-the worst, little-less-the least.

Vocabulary

Spelling and symbols (@ at, . dot, _ underscore), food groups, cooking methods, flavors and emotions with -ed / -ing.
